text:
anya: Heads-up — intermittent KV-cache divergence on the new q8_int4 bring-up when prefilled with long prefixes (~40–60k tokens). Repro is flaky but fairly reliable on a 4-shard local run. Logs and quick repro below. Anyone seen phase-wander or RoPE scale drift like this?

mike: can you paste the minimal repro and the exact cmd?

anya: repro snippet: 
```
python -m rl.eval harness --model build/q8_int4/v2 --prefill-file long_prefix.txt --seed 42 --shards 4 --steps 512 --dump-kv-ids
```
then tail of kv-dump: 
```
[step 128] kv_index=2345678 expected=2345677 rot_phase_delta=2.9e-04
[step 256] kv_index=2345699 expected=2345699 rot_phase_delta=1.1e-06
[step 384] kv_index=2345901 expected=2345901 rot_phase_delta=3.2e-05
```
behavior: tokens diverge after step ~130, sampled generations differ ~8-12% token-wise vs fp16 baseline.

julia: do you see the same with FP16 loader? any quantization fallback test?

anya: FP16 baseline produces no divergence. I ran quick int8 fallback (runtime knob `--quant-fallback fp16-on-prefill`) — divergence drops to 0.7%.

kevin: sounds like quant noise + phase accumulation. Could be prefill stride causing off-by-one in per-shard KV offsets. Did you try `--kv-stride=1` vs default parallel stride?

anya: yes, with `--kv-stride=1` the repro rate drops but doesn't go away entirely. I also toggled `--rotary-scale=rope_v2` vs `rope_v1` and saw the delta track with v1 being worse.

mike: can you dump the binary kv indices and raw rotary angles for the mismatch step? might be a rounding / memcpy alignment issue on int4 kernels.

anya: attached inline sample (hex blob simplified): `KV_SHARD0: ... 0x7f 0x2a 0x99` and same offset on SHARD1 shows slight byte shift. Noted that mmap alignment is 64-byte on that worker.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Started nightly-eval job #eval-2056 on runner-3 (gpu-a100-40g). Logs -> https://ci.internal/eval/2056

sara: I had a similar symptom last month when a new memcpy path landed in the runtime (memcopy_v2). Could be alignment in the patch that reorders small tiles. @eng-runtime might need to revert memcopy_v2 for a quick check.

kevin: I'm spinning a small experiment: 1) force fp16 prefill, 2) run quantized decode but with `--kv-zero-fill` to detect uninitialized lanes, 3) enable deterministic memcpy (old path). I'll post results in ~30m.

anya: thanks — FYI I also measured per-token latency skew: quant run shows 3–6% extra time at prefill flush, and those moments correlate with first divergence steps.

mike: can you also run with `--trace-id=<uuid>` so we can join with console traces? add `--trace-collect=kvcaches`

anya: started a run with trace-id 9a1b-4c3d. Dumped trace link: https://console.internal/traces/9a1b-4c3d. Key event: shard swap at prefill boundary logged as "kv-window-commit" with duration spikes.

julia: if shard swap coincides with rotary angle update we might be applying different phase scaling to cached keys vs newly computed keys. That would create deterministic but invisible drift once quantized.

kevin: experiment results:
- fp16-prefill + q8 decode: no divergence after 1k steps (good)
- fp16-prefill + q8 + kv-zero-fill: small mismatches still at 0.4% (likely rounding)
- quant prefill + deterministic-memcpy: repro rate fell from ~60% to ~12%

kevin: so memcopy timing/alignment + quant prefill seems multiplicative. I'm going to push a diagnostic build with explicit 128-byte pinned align and small assert to check boundary writes.

anya: thanks. If that reduces to <1% we can ship a stability mitigation: prefer fp16 prefill on long-prefix workloads until int4 prefill kernels are hardened.

mike: also add a targeted unit test to eval harness: generate 4-shard run with deterministic seed + artificially induce a shard swap at a known token index, then compare kv indices across replicas bitwise. That should catch this class earlier.

sara: +1 on the unit test. I'll file a tiny RFC to add prefill-hardened mode to Dedicated configs for customers with long-context SLAs.

anya: opened ticket ENG-ML-9241 with repro script and links to traces + dump. I'll update here when kevin's diagnostic build lands. :thumbsup:

mike: great. If anyone needs GPU cycles ping me; I'll reserve runner-3 for repros for the next 6h.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Diagnostic build 2056-rc2 deployed to runner-3 (memcopy pin + assert).

kevin: rc2 reduced repro to ~1.1% on my 8 repeats. Pushing PR to runtime to enable pinned-copy by default for int4 prefill.

anya: verified on my longer prefix too — divergence now at noise floor. Marking as mitigated for bring-up. Will add notes to model onboarding checklist about prefilling mode recommendations.

mike: excellent — thanks everyone.
